'''Nenad Krstić''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Ненад Крстић}}, born July 25, 1983) is a Serbian [[basketball]] executive and former professional player.

Krstić represented and [[Captain (sports)|captained]] the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbian national basketball team]] internationally. Standing at 2.12 m (7 ft 0 in), he played the [[center (basketball)|center]] position. Krstić was an [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] member in [[2004–05 NBA season|2005]] and a two-time
[[All-Euroleague First Team]] selection in [[2011–12 Euroleague|2012]] and [[2012–13 Euroleague|2013]].

==Professional career==

===Partizan Belgrade===
His first professional team was [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]] where he spent four seasons, making his debut in 2000–01. In the 2003–04 season, his last with Partizan, he averaged 13.4 points per game in the [[2003–04 Euroleague|Euroleague]]. With Partizan, he also won three [[YUBA League]] championships in a row, and one [[Kup Radivoja Koraća|Serbian Cup]] championship in the 2001–02 season.

On June 26, 2002, he was drafted with the 24th overall pick in the [[2002 NBA draft]] by the [[New Jersey Nets]]. However, he didn't join the Nets for two seasons, continuing to play with Partizan Belgrade.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hoopshype.com/players/nenad_krstic.htm |title=NBA Players – Nenad Krstic |publisher=HoopsHype.com |access-date=2007-04-24}}</ref>

===New Jersey Nets===
During the [[2004–05 NBA season]], Krstić logged an impressive rookie campaign for the New Jersey Nets, averaging 10.0 points, 5.3 rebounds and 0.84 blocked shots per game.<ref name="stats">{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/nenad_krstic/career_stats.html |title=Nenad Krstic Info Page – Career Stats and Totals |publisher=NBA.com |access-date=2007-04-24 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070427085102/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/nenad_krstic/career_stats.html |archive-date=2007-04-27 }}</ref> He was honored as part of the All-Rookie NBA second team.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/krstic_050505.html |title=Krstic Named to NBA All-Rookie Second Team |date=2005-05-05 |publisher=Nets.com |access-date=2007-04-24}}</ref>

In his debut in the [[NBA Playoffs|playoffs]] against the [[Miami Heat]], Krstić averaged 18.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 1.0 assists per game;<ref name="stats"/> an exceptional performance for a rookie in the playoffs. This followed a greater trend where Krstić had consistently improved at a great pace as his rookie season progressed. He showed a wide skill set for a big man, including refined post moves and a  shooting touch from eighteen feet.

Throughout the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]], Krstić's play had continued to rapidly improve. Three quarters of the way through the season, he averaged 13.4 points and 6.1 rebounds, and had become an integral part of the Nets offense. In the first round of the 2006 NBA playoffs against Indiana he averaged 18 points per game along with 7.1 rebounds.

In [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07]] despite the rough Nets start, Krstić was averaging career-highs in points (16.6), rebounds (6.8), and assists (1.8)<ref name="stats"/> before falling to the ground after tearing his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] in his left knee versus the [[Los Angeles Lakers|L.A. Lakers]] at [[Continental Airlines Arena]] on December 22, 2006.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2707261 |title=Nets center Krstic has torn ACL, out for year |date=2006-12-23 |work=ESPN.com |access-date=2007-04-24}}</ref> His surgery was successful.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/krstic_surgery.html |title=Krstic Has Successful Surgery |date=2005-05-03 |publisher=Nets.com |access-date=2007-04-24}}</ref> Krstić was out for the rest of the [[2006–07 NBA season]], but returned ahead of schedule to start the [[2007–08 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/chat/krstic_chat_transcript_011508.html |title=NBA.com New Jersey Nets Home |publisher=NBA.com |access-date=2008-02-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080118074020/http://www.nba.com/nets/chat/krstic_chat_transcript_011508.html |archive-date=2008-01-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

His 2007–08 season was a disappointment, as his injury disrupted his play and confidence on the court and he was largely a liability. Krstić later stated in his blog that he felt he let the team down, and vowed to return to his old form at the start of the 08–09 season.

===Triumph Lyubertsy===
During the 2008 summer off-season, Krstić entered negotiations with the [[Russian Basketball Super League|Russian Super League]] team [[BC Triumph Lyubertsy|Triumph Lyubertsy]] and eventually signed a 2-year contract (with the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] an opt-out option) worth [[Euro|€]]6 million euros [[net income]] with them on July 29, 2008.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/nets/2008/07/28/2008-07-28_nenad_krstic_signs_deal_with_russian_tea.html |title=Nenad Krstić signs deal with Russian team in Moscow |date=2008-07-29 |publisher=nydailynews.com |access-date=2008-07-29 }}{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Ford |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3508955 |title=Kristic signs with Triumph for 2 years $18 million USD |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2008-07-29 |access-date=2012-04-24}}</ref> He averaged 10.4 points and 5.1 rebounds per game in seven games in the Russian Super League<ref name="Triumph">{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130117180701/http://www.bctriumph.com/news/archive/archive_360.html|title=Triumph Center Nenad Krstic will play for NBA.}}</ref><ref name="Triumph stats">[http://www.basket.ru/index.php?dn=team&to=stats&id=2135&ml=1&co=4025 Триумф (Люберцы, Московская область) » СУММАРНАЯ СТАТИСТИКА.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081222225750/http://www.basket.ru/index.php?dn=team&to=stats&id=2135&ml=1&co=4025 |date=December 22, 2008 }}</ref>  and 13.3 points and 7.3 rebounds per game in 6 games in the [[EuroChallenge]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.playerID_36172.compID_BYg5Rb55Jw-G5I3MZ6JB01.season_2009.roundID_6491.teamID_97051.html |title=Krstić EuroChallenge stats |publisher=Fibaeurope.com |access-date=2012-04-24}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder===
On December 19, 2008, two NBA league sources told ESPN.com that the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] had agreed in principle to sign Krstić to a three-year offer sheet.<ref>{{cite web|author=Chad Ford |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3782171 |title=Sources: Krstic, Thunder agree to deal |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2008-12-19 |access-date=2012-04-24}}</ref> On December 22, Krstić officially signed the offer sheet. The New Jersey Nets had seven days to match the offer, or Krstić would be free to join the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3788805 |title=Thunder sign Krstic to offer sheet |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2008-12-22 |access-date=2012-04-24}}</ref> The Nets declined to match, and the Thunder waived [[Steven Hill (basketball)|Steven Hill]] to make room for Krstić.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3800161 |title=Krstic gives Thunder another 7-footer |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2008-12-30 |access-date=2012-04-24}}</ref>

He played for the first time in a Thunder uniform on January 7, 2009, versus the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], scoring six points and blocking 2 shots in 16 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|author=Target Center, Minneapolis|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290107016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090123133610/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290107016 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 23, 2009 |title=Foye, Wolves beat Thunder for fourth straight victory |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2009-01-07 |access-date=2012-04-24}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics===
On February 24, 2011, Krstić was traded along with [[Jeff Green (basketball)|Jeff Green]] and a 2012 first-round pick to the [[Boston Celtics]] for [[Kendrick Perkins]] and [[Nate Robinson]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Ford|first1=Chad|title=Celtics get Thunder's Jeff Green|url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/news/story?id=6155082|access-date=4 November 2014|publisher=ESPN|date=25 February 2011}}</ref> In his first game as a Celtic, he recorded 9 points and 6 rebounds in a win against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on February 26.<ref>{{cite news|title=New-look Celtics rally for 4th win in last 5 games|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310226012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110303002207/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310226012|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 3, 2011|access-date=4 November 2014|publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

Krstić's final NBA game was on May 11, 2011, in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals against the [[Miami Heat]]. Boston would lose that game 87 - 97 (thus losing the series to Miami 4 - 1) with Krstić recording 8 points, 2 rebounds and 2 blocks.

===CSKA Moscow===
On June 22, 2011, Krstić signed a two-year contract with the Russian powerhouse [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2011-12-signings/i/86052/5611/cska-puts-veteran-krstic-at-center |title=CSKA puts veteran Krstic at center |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=2011-06-22 |access-date=2012-04-24}}</ref> Over the [[2011–12 Euroleague|season]], he averaged 14.2 points and 5.4 rebounds in 24.5 minutes per game in the [[Euroleague Basketball|Euroleague]]. That earned him his first selection for the [[All-Euroleague First Team]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2011-12 All-Euroleague First, Second teams announced|url=http://www.euroleague.net/final-four/istanbul-2012/main-page/i/97498/7005/2011-12-all-euroleague-first-second-teams-announced|work=Euroleague.net|access-date=15 August 2013}}</ref> In the [[Euroleague Final]] against [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], CSKA Moscow lost by 61–62 after [[Georgios Printezis]]'s [[buzzer beater]] in the last seconds of the game, securing his team second Euroleague championship in history.<ref>{{cite web|title=Olympiacos is the Euroleague winner|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/cups/euroleague/38589/olympiacos-is-the-euroleague-winner.html|work=Sportando|access-date=3 February 2014}}</ref>

yet'|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/39455/nenad-krstic-i-have-nba-options-but-i-haven-t-decided-yet.html|work=Sportando}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Farnsworth|first=Nick|title=NBA Rumors: Is Nenad Krstic Considering a Return to the Boston Celtics?|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1251369-is-nenad-krstic-considering-a-return-to-the-boston-celtics|work=Bleacher web|title=Teodosić: Sami smo krivi|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/vesti.php?yyyy=2014&mm=05&dd=17&nav_id=849235|work=b92.net|access-date=20 May 2014|language=sr}}</ref> Krstić finished his third Shortly after the Final 4, CSKA was facing elimination in the [[2013–14 VTB United League|VTB United League]] from [[PBC Lokomotiv-Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]], travelling by 2-0 without home advantage. Krstić helped CSKA eventually win the series after big comeback and advance to semifinals, answering to previous critics of the club's president. Eventually, CSKA won the VTB United League by sweeping [[BC Nizhny Novgorod|Nizhny Novgorod]] 3–0 in the final series.<ref>{{cite web|title=CSKA crowned champions!!!|url=http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-crowned-champions.htm|website=vtb-league.com|access-date=14 June 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140617172025/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-crowned-champions.htm|archive-date=17 June 2014}}</ref>

In the late June, CSKA Moscow used option in his contract to part ways and allow him to sign with another team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hvala, Nenad!|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=13532&lang=en|website=cskabasket.com|access-date=24 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Nenad Krstic leaves CSKA Moscow|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/123874/nenad-krstic-leaves-cska-moscow.html|website=sportando.net|access-date=24 June 2014}}</ref> In July 2014, weeks after signing with Anadolu Efes, he had an interview for ''[[Večernje novosti]]''. He stated that [[Ettore Messina]], former coach of CSKA Moscow, was "killing him as a player", putting him to play at unnatural to him [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position, which affected on his performances over the last two seasons with the club.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Jakovljević|first1=I.|title=Krstić: Mesina me "ubijao"|url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.295.html:502529-Krstic-Mesina-me-ubijao|website=novosti.rs|access-date=26 July 2014|language=sr}}</ref>

===Anadolu Efes===
On June 26, 2014, Krstić signed a two-year contract with the Turkish team [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Anadolu Efes goes big with Krstic|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/138164|access-date=June 26, 2014|work=Euroleague.net|date=June 26, 2014}}</ref> He came in the club just after [[Dušan Ivković]] was appointed as new head coach, with whom he worked in the national team for many years.

;2014–15 season
On November 2, 2014, he fractured his left forearm, after [[flagrant foul]] by Mutlu Demir, in a game against [[Pınar Karşıyaka]] and was estimated to return in 6 to 8 weeks.<ref>{{cite news|title=Anadolu Efes center Nenad Krstic of Serbia will be out for at least 6 weeks with a broken left forearm|url=http://www.trt.net.tr/english/sports/2014/11/03/efes-big-man-krstic-out-for-6-to-8-weeks-with-broken-arm-105580|access-date=3 November 2014|work=trt.net.tr}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Efes big man Nenad Krstic out 6-8 weeks with broken arm|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/139800/efes-big-man-nenad-krstic-out-6-8-weeks-with-broken-arm.html|access-date=3 November 2014|work=sportando.com}}</ref> He returned on the court on December 24, in a game against [[Darüşşafaka S.K.|Darüşşafaka Doğuş]] and scored 2 points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Anadolu Efes 73 - 72 Darussafaka Dogus, December 24, 2014|url=https://www.tblstat.net/game/15591|website=TBLStat.net}}</ref>

As the season was reaching to an end, Anadolu Efes cemented second position of the regular season in the [[2014–15 Turkish Basketball League|Turkish League]]. However, they were stopped in the [[2014–15 Euroleague|Euroleague]] after the [[2014–15 Euroleague Quarter-finals|quarter-final]] series 1–3 loss to the eventual champion [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].

On June 14, 2015, in a Game 3 of the Turkish League final series against [[Karşıyaka Basket|Pınar Karşıyaka]], he tore [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] on his right knee.<ref>{{cite news|title=Geçmiş olsun Krstic...|url=https://www.anadoluefessk.org/haber/gecmis-olsun-krstic-1|access-date=15 June 2015|work=anadoluefessk.org|language=tr}}</ref> The injury will keep him off-the-court for estimated 6 months.

Over the season, he averaged 12.4 points and 5.2 rebounds in 27 games played of the Turkish League. He also played in 19 Euroleague games, where he averaged 12.8 points, 5.1 rebounds and a career-high 1.4 assists per game.

===Galatasaray Odeabank===
On June 30, 2016, Krstić signed with Turkish club [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray Odeabank]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nenad Krstic Galatasaray Odeabank'ta|url=http://www.galatasaray.org/haber/basketbol/erkek-basketbol/nenad-krstic-galatasaray-odeabank-ta/32715|date=30 June 2016|access-date=30 June 2016|work=galatasaray.org|language=tr}}</ref> On September 9, 2016, he parted ways with Galatasaray.<ref>{{cite news|title=Galata potvrdila: Krstićev ugovor raskinut|url=http://mondo.rs/a937676/Sport/Kosarka/Galatasaraj-Raskinut-ugovor-Nenada-Krstica.html|access-date=13 April 2017|work=mondo.rs|date=9 September 2016|language=sr}}</ref>

==National team career==
Krstić played with the [[Serbia and Montenegro national basketball team|Serbia and Montenegro national team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics|2004 Summer Olympics]] and [[EuroBasket 2005]].

As captain of [[Serbia national basketball team|Serbian national team]] he played at the [[EuroBasket 2009]], where he won the silver medal and [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], where he won the fourth place. In the following year, he played at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]] where Serbia was defeated 99–88 by [[Lithuania]] in the game for the bronze medal. He represented the national team at the [[EuroBasket 2011]] in Lithuania where Serbia finished eighth and at the [[EuroBasket 2013]] in Slovenia where Serbia finished seventh and qualified for [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. At the World Cup in Spain, Serbian national team took the silver medal. Shortly after the final game of the tournament, he retired from the national team, after ten years of playing and six years of captaining.<ref>{{cite news|title=Krstić se oprostio od reprezentacije|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/spanija2014/vesti.php?yyyy=2014&mm=09&dd=15&nav_id=899806|access-date=15 September 2014|work=b92.net|language=sr}}</ref>

== Post-playing career ==
On August 22, 2019, Krstić was named a director of the youth national basketball teams at the [[Basketball Federation of Serbia]] (KSS).<ref>{{cite web |title=Nenad Krstić postao direktor mlađih selekcija Srbije |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2019&mm=08&dd=22&nav_id=1581072 |website=b92.net |access-date=22 August 2019}}</ref> On December 14, 2020, Krstić was elected vice-president of the Basketball Federation of Serbia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Daniloviću novi mandat, Krstić potpredsednik |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2020&mm=12&dd=14&nav_id=1780659 |website=b92.net}}</ref>

After stepping down from his position at Basketball Federation of Serbia, Krstić was named the president of his hometown team [[KK Sloga|KK Sloga Kraljevo]].

==Personal life==
Krstić is married to his wife Tanja and has one daughter.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mondo.rs/s186037/Zvezde_i_tracevi/Nenad_Krstic_postao_otac.html |title=Nenad Krstić postao otac | Mondo |publisher=Mondo.rs |date=2010-06-10 |access-date=2012-04-24}}</ref> Krstić, whose nickname is "Curly", was voted the third most eligible bachelor by Serbia's version of [[People (magazine)|''People'' magazine]].<ref name=curly>{{cite web |url=http://deadspin.com/sports/nba/five-tiny-tidbits-on-the-new-jersey-nets-210952.php |title=Five Tiny Tidbits On: The New Jersey Nets |date=2006-10-30 |publisher=Deadspin |access-date=2007-04-24}}</ref>
On August 19, 2010, in a game against Greece for the [[Acropolis International Tournament 2010]], he participated in a fight between players and threw a chair at Greek [[Ioannis Bourousis]]. That resulted in his spending the night at the police station, from where he was released the day after.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5478923 |title=Police release Nenad Krstic after melee |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> He stated in his defence that he thought Bourousis was a fan when he threw the chair at him. In the same fight Krstić attacked Greek player [[Sofoklis Schortsanitis]] a number of times from behind.

After the [[2010 Serbia earthquake]], Krstić and his [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] teammates donated $10,000 to help his hometown of [[Kraljevo]], which was directly affected by the nearby calamity.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5779054 |title=Nenad Krstic, Oklahoma City Thunder raising money for victims of Serbian earthquake - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2010-11-07 |access-date=2012-04-24}}</ref>

Krstić owns and operates a [[distillery]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Intervju, Uroš Tripković: Od "bloka za Uroša" do plantaža borovnica |url=https://moravainfo.rs/2019/01/intervju-uros-tripkovic-od-bloka-za-urosa-do-plantaza-borovnica/ |website=moravainfo.rs |access-date=5 March 2019 |language=sr |archive-date=March 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306043853/https://moravainfo.rs/2019/01/intervju-uros-tripkovic-od-bloka-za-urosa-do-plantaza-borovnica/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
